nameStory: The dragon's mouth orchid gets its dramatic name from its distinctive flower, which resembles a mythical dragon opening its mouth wide. The single pink bloom has a prominent lip that looks like a tongue, fringed with white and yellow 'teeth' that complete the fierce dragon appearance.
description: Dragon's mouth orchid is a rare and enchanting native orchid that produces a single, spectacular pink flower. This small terrestrial orchid grows only about 6 inches tall from a underground bulb. The solitary flower sits atop a slender stem with typically just one narrow leaf, creating an elegant and unmistakable silhouette in wet habitats.

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Single large pink flower with a prominent, inflated lower lip that has white and yellow fringed crests - looks like a dragon's open mouth with decorative teeth

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Usually just one narrow, grass-like leaf that emerges after flowering, though sometimes absent during bloom time

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Solitary orchid growing about 6 inches tall from boggy ground, with one flower per plant on a slender, smooth stem

idTips.label: Habitat Clue
idTips.description: Always found in very wet, acidic conditions like sphagnum bogs where your feet will sink into spongy moss

habitat: Dragon's mouth orchid thrives in acidic wetlands including sphagnum bogs, swamps, and wet meadows throughout New England. Look for it in areas with consistently moist, peaty soil where sphagnum moss dominates and the ground feels spongy underfoot. These habitats are often associated with cranberries, pitcher plants, and other bog specialists.

seasonality.spring: The dramatic pink flowers appear in late spring to early summer (May-July), often emerging before the leaf fully develops.
seasonality.summer: After flowering, a single narrow leaf emerges and photosynthesizes through the summer, storing energy in the underground bulb.
seasonality.fall: The leaf yellows and dies back, leaving no visible trace above ground as the plant enters dormancy.
seasonality.winter: Completely dormant underground with no visible parts - the bulb waits beneath the frozen bog surface.

funFact: This orchid is so rare and specialized that it can disappear for years at a time, remaining dormant underground when conditions aren't perfect, then suddenly reappear like magic when the bog habitat is just right.
confusionNotes: Dragon's mouth is unlikely to be confused with other plants due to its unique flower shape and bog habitat. The distinctive dragon-mouth appearance of the pink flower with fringed white and yellow lip is unmistakable among New England orchids.
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called dragon's mouth orchid, this plant is named after Arethusa, a water nymph from Greek mythology who was transformed into a spring - fitting for an orchid that loves wet places. It's the only species in its genus worldwide.
compareHints: As the sole species in the Arethusa genus, dragon's mouth is unique among orchids. Compared to other New England bog orchids like grass pink or rose pogonia, dragon's mouth is distinguished by its much larger, more inflated flower lip and the dramatic fringed crests that create its namesake dragon appearance.
